In `HTTPServer.HTTPServer()`: HttpServer is a Vert.x-based HTTP server implementation with direct WebSocket transport support. It uses the webSocketHandler approach where any HTTP request can be upgraded to WebSocket, eliminating the need for clients to open local HTTP servers.

This implementation follows the direct WebSocket approach where:

  • Server accepts WebSocket upgrades on any HTTP request
  • Clients connect using WebSocket protocol directly
  • Bidirectional communication over WebSocket connections
  • Client registration by event topic
  • Message sending with round-robin load balancing
  • Periodic keep-alive signals to connected clients

Key features:

  • Direct WebSocket handler for simple setup
  • Topic-based client registration and message routing
  • Round-robin load balancing for multiple clients on same topic
  • Automatic keep-alive mechanism
  • No SSL support (as requested)
  • Integration with Vert.x EventBus
/ public class HTTPServer implements TransportServer { // HTTP server configuration (host, port, event type, etc.) private final JsonObject config; // Event type associated with this HTTP server private final String eventType; // Vert.x HttpServer instance private HttpServer server; // Logger instance for HTTP server private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(HttpServer.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_EVENT_BUS, "HTTP Server"); // Map of event topic → list of connected WebSocket connections private final Map> connections = new HashMap<>(); // Round-robin index for each topic private final Map indexes = new HashMap<>(); // Timer ID for keep-alive scheduling private long timer; / Constructs an HttpServer instance with the given configuration. @param config JSON configuration containing server details like port and event type.

In `DNSUtil.resolve()`: DNS Utility class that provides comprehensive DNS resolution services for the Motadata platform.

This class extends {@link AbstractVerticle} and serves as the central DNS management component, handling both forward and reverse DNS lookups, DNS cache management, and DNS server profile configuration. It automatically discovers system DNS servers and provides event-driven DNS resolution services.

Key Features:

  • Automatic discovery and configuration of system DNS servers
  • Forward DNS resolution (hostname to IP)
  • Reverse DNS resolution (IP to hostname)
  • DNS cache management and flushing
  • Multiple DNS server profile support with fallback mechanism
  • Event-driven architecture for asynchronous DNS operations
  • Integration with Motadata's object management system

DNS Server Priority:

DNS servers are prioritized with automatic (system-discovered) servers taking precedence over manually configured ones. The class implements a fallback mechanism where if one DNS server fails to resolve a query, it automatically tries the next available server.

/ public class DNSUtil extends AbstractVerticle { private static final Logger LOGGER = new Logger(DNSUtil.class, GlobalConstants.MOTADATA_UTIL, "DNS Util"); / Initializes the DNS resolver module and sets up the complete DNS management infrastructure.

This method serves as the entry point for the DNS utility service, performing comprehensive initialization of DNS server profiles, event bus consumers, and system integration. It automatically discovers system DNS servers and configures them as default profiles if they don't already exist.

Initialization Process:

  1. System DNS Discovery: Uses {@link ResolverConfig#getCurrentConfig()} to discover DNS servers configured in the system's network settings
  2. Profile Creation: For each discovered DNS server, checks if a profile already exists in {@code DNSServerProfileConfigStore}. If not, creates a new profile with default settings
  3. Database Persistence: Saves new DNS profiles to the database table {@code TBL_DNS_SERVER_PROFILE} with automatic resolver type
  4. Event Bus Registration: Sets up local consumers for all DNS-related events

Event Bus Consumers Registered:

  • {@code EVENT_DNS_SERVER_RESOLVER}: Triggers bulk DNS resolution for all cached IPs and objects
  • {@code EVENT_DNS_OBJECT_DELETE}: Handles cleanup when objects are deleted from the system
  • {@code EVENT_DNS_LOOKUP}: Performs forward DNS lookup for a single hostname
  • {@code EVENT_DNS_REVERSE_LOOKUP}: Performs reverse DNS lookup for a single IP address
  • {@code EVENT_DNS_CACHE_FLUSH}: Flushes both system and application DNS caches

Extracts and separates static and dynamic tags from the request body.

This method expects the request body (from {@code routingContext.body().asJsonObject()}) to contain a JsonArray under the key {@link #TAG_RULE_TAGS}. Each element in that array may be:

  • a static tag (stored as-is), or
  • a dynamic tag following the {@code PATTERN} (example: {@code host:{object.host}}).
Behavior:
  1. Iterate over the incoming tags.
  2. If a tag matches {@code PATTERN}, extract the left-hand side as the dynamic tag key and the inner token as the dynamic tag value and add to {@code TAG_RULE_DYNAMIC_TAGS}.
  3. Otherwise collect the tag as a static tag and resolve it using {@link TagConfigStore#getStore()#addItems(JsonArray, String, String)} which returns the stored representation (hash/ids) for static tags.
  4. Update the original request body in-place with resolved static tags and dynamic tags.
The returned JsonObject is the same object as the request body (modified in-place) and is annotated as non-null. @param routingContext Vert.x routing context containing the request body @return modified request body JsonObject with {@code TAG_RULE_TAGS} and {@code TAG_RULE_DYNAMIC_TAGS} populated

Listens for incoming network flow data and forwards it for processing.

The FlowListener is responsible for receiving network flow data from various sources, such as sFlow and NetFlow, and forwarding it to the FlowProcessor for further processing. It acts as the entry point for flow data into the system.

Key responsibilities of this class include:

  • Starting and managing flow collector processes for different flow types (sFlow, NetFlow)
  • Configuring the flow collectors based on settings from the FlowSettingsConfigStore
  • Managing the lifecycle of flow collector processes
  • Handling port configurations for different flow protocols
  • Ensuring proper cleanup of resources when stopping

The FlowListener supports multiple flow protocols and can be configured to listen on different ports for each protocol. It also supports BGP-enabled flow collection for enhanced routing information.

This class is deployed as a Vert.x verticle and integrates with the event bus system for communication with other components.

The StreamingBroadcaster is responsible for broadcasting streaming data to connected clients.

This class works in conjunction with the StreamingEngine to:

  • Manage streaming sessions for different types of streaming data
  • Apply filtering logic to streaming data based on client preferences
  • Enrich streaming data with additional context information
  • Broadcast streaming data to the appropriate clients
  • Enforce limits on the number of concurrent streaming sessions

The StreamingBroadcaster supports multiple types of streaming (defined in {@link StreamingEngine.StreamingType}) and maintains separate session maps for each type to ensure proper isolation and management.

This class is implemented as a Vert.x verticle and uses the Vert.x event bus for communication with other components in the system.

This class handles:

  • Network topology discovery using various protocols (SNMP, CDP, LLDP, etc.)
  • Building dependency maps between network devices
  • Tracking connections between network elements
  • Managing worker allocation for topology discovery jobs
  • Processing topology discovery events and responses
  • Notifying users about topology discovery results

The engine supports both Layer 2 (L2) and Layer 3 (L3) topology discovery and can handle various network protocols. It implements a worker pool model to efficiently process topology discovery requests in parallel while managing system resources.

Manages dependencies between IT components in the system.

The DependencyManager is responsible for:

  • Storing and maintaining dependency relationships between components
  • Adding, removing, and querying dependencies
  • Managing dependency connections at different levels
  • Handling special dependency types (e.g., Cisco UCS)
  • Serializing and deserializing dependency data

This manager maintains a complex data structure (Map<String, Map<Byte, Set<Integer>>>) to represent dependencies between entities at different levels. The outer map uses source IPs/targets as keys, the middle map uses dependency levels as keys, and the inner set contains hash codes of destination IPs/targets.

The dependency information stored by this manager is used by other components like the AvailabilityCorrelationEngine and DependencyQueryProcessor to understand relationships between components and make intelligent decisions based on those relationships.

    private void calculateInterfaceMetricRate(long id, String metricKey, JsonObject rateMetrics, Map<String, java.lang.Object> context, long uptime, String objectName)
    {
        try
        {

            var currentTimestamp = DateTimeUtil.currentSeconds();

            var currentSentBytes = CommonUtil.getLong(context.get(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_SENT_OCTETS));//octet means Bytes

            var currentReceivedBytes = CommonUtil.getLong(context.get(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_RECEIVED_OCTETS));//octet means Bytes

            if (contextsByMetric.get(id).get(metricKey) != null)
            {
                metricRateContext = contextsByMetric.get(id).get(metricKey);

                var previousUptime = metricRateContext.get(NMSConstants.STARTED_TIME);

                if (uptime >= previousUptime)
                {
                    var previousSentBytes = metricRateContext.get(NMSConstants.METRIC_ENRICHER_CALCULATOR_SENT_BYTES);

                    var previousReceivedBytes = metricRateContext.get(NMSConstants.METRIC_ENRICHER_CALCULATOR_RECEIVE_BYTES);

                    var previousTimestamp = metricRateContext.get(TIME_STAMP);

                    var interfaceBitType = CommonUtil.getInteger(context.get(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_BIT_TYPE));

                    var pollTimeDifference = currentTimestamp - previousTimestamp;//time difference between two poll times in seconds

                    var interfaceSpeed = CommonUtil.getFloat(context.get(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_SPEED_BYTES_PER_SEC));

                    if (currentSentBytes > previousSentBytes)
                    {
                        calculateInterfaceBandwidth(currentSentBytes, previousSentBytes, pollTimeDifference, rateMetrics, NMSConstants.INTERFACE_OUT_TRAFFIC_BYTES_PER_SEC, interfaceSpeed);
                    }
                    else
                    {

                        if (interfaceBitType == NMSConstants.INTERFACE_COUNTER_TYPE_32_BIT)//for 32 bit interface rollover
                        {
                            if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled())
                            {
                                LOGGER.trace(String.format("interface metric has been rolled over for interface %s of object %s", context.get(NMSConstants.INTERFACE), objectName));
                            }

                            currentSentBytes += NMSConstants.MAX_INTERFACE_SPEED_32_BIT;

                            if (currentSentBytes > previousSentBytes)
                            {

                                calculateInterfaceBandwidth(currentSentBytes, previousSentBytes, pollTimeDifference, rateMetrics, NMSConstants.INTERFACE_OUT_TRAFFIC_BYTES_PER_SEC, interfaceSpeed);
                            }
                        }
                    }

                    if (currentReceivedBytes > previousReceivedBytes)
                    {
                        calculateInterfaceBandwidth(currentReceivedBytes, previousReceivedBytes, pollTimeDifference, rateMetrics, NMSConstants.INTERFACE_IN_TRAFFIC_BYTES_PER_SEC, interfaceSpeed);
                    }

                    else
                    {

                        if (interfaceBitType == NMSConstants.INTERFACE_COUNTER_TYPE_32_BIT)//for 32 bit interface rollover
                        {
                            if (CommonUtil.traceEnabled())
                            {
                                LOGGER.trace(String.format("interface metric has been rolled over for interface %s of object %s", context.get(NMSConstants.INTERFACE), objectName));
                            }

                            currentReceivedBytes += NMSConstants.MAX_INTERFACE_SPEED_32_BIT;

                            if (currentReceivedBytes > previousReceivedBytes)
                            {

                                calculateInterfaceBandwidth(currentSentBytes, previousSentBytes, pollTimeDifference, rateMetrics, NMSConstants.INTERFACE_IN_TRAFFIC_BYTES_PER_SEC, interfaceSpeed);
                            }
                        }
                    }

                    rateMetrics.put(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_TRAFFIC_BYTES_PER_SEC, CommonUtil.getFloat(rateMetrics.getValue(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_IN_TRAFFIC_BYTES_PER_SEC)) + CommonUtil.getFloat(rateMetrics.getValue(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_OUT_TRAFFIC_BYTES_PER_SEC)));

                    rateMetrics.put(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_TRAFFIC_UTILIZATION, CommonUtil.getFloat((CommonUtil.getFloat(rateMetrics.getValue(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_OUT_TRAFFIC_UTILIZATION)) + CommonUtil.getFloat(rateMetrics.getValue(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_IN_TRAFFIC_UTILIZATION))) / 2));
                }

                else

            metricRateContext.put(TIME_STAMP, currentTimestamp);

            metricRateContext.put(NMSConstants.METRIC_ENRICHER_CALCULATOR_SENT_BYTES, currentSentBytes);

            metricRateContext.put(NMSConstants.METRIC_ENRICHER_CALCULATOR_RECEIVE_BYTES, currentReceivedBytes);

            metricRateContext.put(NMSConstants.STARTED_TIME, uptime);

        }

        {

                rateMetrics.put(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_OUT_TRAFFIC_BYTES_PER_SEC, result);

                rateMetrics.put(NMSConstants.INTERFACE_OUT_TRAFFIC_UTILIZATION, calculateInterfaceUtilization(result, interfaceSpeed));
            }

            else

            }

    @RepeatedIfExceptionsTest(suspend = 3000L)
    @Order(1)
    void testSyncSlack(VertxTestContext testContext)
    {
        var credential = TestConstants.prepareParams("testSlackCredentialProfile");

        Assertions.assertNotNull(credential);

        credential.put(CredentialProfile.CREDENTIAL_PROFILE_NAME, credential.getString(CredentialProfile.CREDENTIAL_PROFILE_NAME) + System.currentTimeMillis());

        TestAPIUtil.createCredentialProfile(credential, testContext).onComplete(result ->
        {
            if (result.succeeded())
            {
                var credentialId = result.result();

                var payload = new JsonObject("{\"id\":10000000000005,\"_type\":\"0\",\"integration.type\":\"Slack\",\"integration.context\":{\"target\":\"http://localhost:6334/integration-test/slack/200/api/\",\"timeout\":60,\"auto.sync\":\"off\",\"proxy.enabled\":\"no\",\"sync.interval\":2,\"alert.reoccurrence.action\":\"create\",\"integration.credential.profile\":90469363433},\"integration.attributes\":{}}");

                if (credentialId != null && credentialId != 0)
                {
                    payload.getJsonObject(Integration.INTEGRATION_CONTEXT).put(IntegrationProfile.INTEGRATION_CREDENTIAL_PROFILE, credentialId);

                    TestAPIUtil.put(INTEGRATION_API_ENDPOINT + "/" + 10000000000005L, payload, response ->
                    {
                        if (response.succeeded())
                        {
                            try
                            {
                                testContext.awaitCompletion(3, TimeUnit.SECONDS);

                                var context = new JsonObject().put(EVENT_TYPE, UI_ACTION_INTEGRATION_SYNC)
                                        .put(Integration.INTEGRATION_TYPE, IntegrationConstants.IntegrationType.SLACK.getName())
                                        .put(APIConstants.SESSION_ID, TestUtil.getSessionId())
                                        .put(ID, IntegrationConstants.IntegrationId.SLACK.getName());

                                assertIntegrationSyncTestResult(testContext, STATUS_SUCCEED, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_SUCCESS);

                                TestUtil.vertx().eventBus().send(UI_ACTION_INTEGRATION_SYNC, context);
                            }
                            catch (Exception exception)
                            {
                                LOGGER.error(exception);

                                testContext.failNow(exception);
                            }
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            LOGGER.error(response.cause());

                            testContext.failNow(response.cause());
                        }
                    });
                }
                else
                {
                    testContext.failNow("not able to create credential profile");
                }
            }
            else
            {
                LOGGER.error(result.cause());

                testContext.failNow(result.cause());
            }
        });
    }

    @RepeatedIfExceptionsTest(suspend = 3000L)
    @Order(2)
    void testSyncSlackInvalid(VertxTestContext testContext)
    {
        var payload = new JsonObject("{\"id\":10000000000005,\"_type\":\"0\",\"integration.type\":\"Slack\",\"integration.context\":{\"target\":\"http://localhost:6334/integration-test/slack/400/api/\",\"timeout\":60,\"auto.sync\":\"off\",\"proxy.enabled\":\"no\",\"sync.interval\":2,\"alert.reoccurrence.action\":\"create\",\"integration.credential.profile\":90469363433},\"integration.attributes\":{}}");

        {
            if (response.succeeded())
            {
                try
                {
                    testContext.awaitCompletion(3, TimeUnit.SECONDS);

                    var context = new JsonObject().put(EVENT_TYPE, UI_ACTION_INTEGRATION_SYNC)
                            .put(Integration.INTEGRATION_TYPE, IntegrationConstants.IntegrationType.SLACK.getName())
                            .put(APIConstants.SESSION_ID, TestUtil.getSessionId())
                            .put(ID, IntegrationConstants.IntegrationId.SLACK.getName());

                    assertIntegrationSyncTestResult(testContext, STATUS_FAIL, ErrorCodes.ERROR_CODE_NO_ITEM_FOUND);

                    TestUtil.vertx().eventBus().send(UI_ACTION_INTEGRATION_SYNC, context);

                catch (Exception exception)
                {
                    LOGGER.error(exception);

                    testContext.failNow(exception);
                }
            }
            else
            {
                LOGGER.error(response.cause());

                testContext.failNow(response.cause());
            }
        }));
    }


    private void assertIntegrationSyncTestResult(VertxTestContext testContext, String status, String errorCode)
    {
        messageConsumer = TestUtil.vertx().eventBus().localConsumer(EVENT_USER + TestUtil.getSessionId(), message -> testContext.verify(() ->
        {
            try
            {
                var event = message.body();

                if (event.containsKey(EVENT_TYPE) && event.getString(EVENT_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(UI_ACTION_INTEGRATION_SYNC))
                {

                    var context = CodecUtil.toJSONObject(message.body().getBinary(EventBusConstants.EVENT_CONTEXT));

                    LOGGER.info(String.format("context received : %s", context.encode()));

                    if (context.containsKey(STATUS) && context.getValue(STATUS) != null)
                    {
                        LOGGER.info(String.format("Integration event for slack successfully with context %s", context.encode()));

                        Assertions.assertEquals(context.getString(STATUS), status);

                        if (errorCode != null)
                        {
                            Assertions.assertEquals(context.getString(ERROR_CODE), errorCode);
                        }

                        messageConsumer.unregister(result -> testContext.completeNow());
                    }

                }
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                messageConsumer.unregister(result -> testContext.failNow(exception));

            }
        }));
    }

Utility class for accessing Motadata application configuration settings.

This class provides centralized access to all configuration parameters used throughout the Motadata application. It loads configuration from a JSON file (motadata.json) and provides getter methods for accessing specific configuration values with appropriate default values when settings are not explicitly configured.

Configuration categories include: - System settings (bootstrap type, environment type, etc.) - Network settings (ports, hosts, timeouts, etc.) - Worker pool sizes for various components - Cache settings and timeouts - Integration settings - Database settings - High availability (HA) settings - Security settings

The class uses a static initializer to load configuration when first accessed, ensuring configuration is available to all components that need it.

Implementation of the Notification abstract class for sending Microsoft Teams notifications.

This class handles Microsoft Teams notifications by sending HTTP requests to the Microsoft Teams API. It supports:

  • Sending messages to multiple Teams channels in parallel
  • Circuit breaker pattern to handle Teams service failures
  • OAuth token authentication with automatic token refresh
  • Severity-based color coding of messages
  • Configurable timeout for Teams API requests

The notification process:

  1. Retrieves Teams integration configuration from the configuration store
  2. Validates that channels are specified and Teams integration is configured
  3. For each channel, retrieves the channel configuration and credential profile
  4. Formats the message with severity-based color coding
  5. Sends HTTP requests to the Teams API for each channel
  6. Handles authentication failures by refreshing OAuth tokens
  7. Tracks successful deliveries and reports results

The notification event should contain:

  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#CHANNELS}: JsonArray of channel IDs to send the message to
  • {@link Notification#CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT}: The message content in Teams card format
  • {@link GlobalConstants#SEVERITY} (optional): The severity level for color coding

This implementation uses a circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures when the Microsoft Teams service is experiencing issues.

A verticle responsible for calculating and managing trace statistics in real-time. This class processes trace events, computes various metrics, and periodically generates service-level key performance indicators (KPIs).

Key features include:

  • Real-time trace statistics calculation
  • Service-level KPI computation (error rates, durations, throughput)
  • Percentile calculations (P50, P99) for trace durations
  • Periodic metrics publishing to event bus
  • Integration with data store for metrics persistence

The calculator processes the following metrics:

  • Total trace count per service
  • Average trace duration
  • Error rates and success counts
  • Throughput (traces per minute)
  • Latency percentiles (P50, P99)

Statistics are calculated and flushed at configurable intervals (default: {@code trace.stat.flush.timer.seconds}). The calculator maintains separate statistics for each service and supports concurrent processing of trace events.

A verticle responsible for listening for log messages over UDP connections.

The UDPLogListener creates a UDP socket that listens on a configured port for incoming log messages. It performs the following tasks:

  • Listens for UDP packets on the configured port
  • Parses incoming log messages
  • Creates log events with metadata (source IP, timestamp, etc.)
  • Forwards log events to the appropriate event bus address
  • Supports streaming log messages for real-time monitoring
  • Tracks log quota usage

The listener can be configured to send logs directly to the log processing pipeline or to a log processor component based on the PROCESSOR_ENABLED setting.

UDP is a connectionless protocol, which makes it suitable for high-volume log collection where some packet loss is acceptable.

The UIActionEventHandler class handles events triggered by user interface actions and routes them to appropriate handlers.

This class is responsible for:

  • Processing UI-initiated events and actions
  • Routing events to appropriate handlers based on event type
  • Enriching events with additional context information
  • Managing notification delivery through various channels (email, integration channels)
  • Validating user inputs and configurations
  • Executing administrative actions (user management, configuration testing, etc.)
  • Handling file uploads and downloads

The handler acts as a bridge between the user interface and the backend systems, translating user actions into system events and routing them to the appropriate components for processing. It also handles the responses from these components and formats them for presentation to the user.

The class supports a wide range of UI actions including:

  • User authentication and authorization
  • Configuration testing (credentials, connections, etc.)
  • Report generation and export
  • Notification management
  • File uploads and downloads
  • System administration tasks

Example usage: 

   // Deploy the UIActionEventHandler   vertx.deployVerticle(new UIActionEventHandler());     // Send a UI action event   JsonObject event = new JsonObject()       .put("action", "test-credential")       .put("credential", credentialJson)       .put("session_id", sessionId);     vertx.eventBus().send("UI_ACTION_CONFIGURATION_TEST", event, reply -> {       if (reply.succeeded()) {           // Handle successful response           JsonObject result = reply.result().body();           System.out.println("Test result: " + result.getString("status"));       } else {           // Handle failure           System.err.println("Test failed: " + reply.cause().getMessage());       }   });

Configuration store for managing user profiles in the system.

This store handles the persistence and retrieval of user profile configurations, which define access scopes and permissions for users. User profiles can be configured with either group-based or tag-based access control mechanisms.

User profiles contain:

  • Profile name and description
  • Associated users
  • Role assignments
  • Scope type (GROUP or TAG)
  • Context-specific access rules

Compares entries of {@code oldProps.getJsonObject(key)} and {@code newProps.getJsonObject(key)} and updates {@code previousContext} and {@code updatedContext} with keys that were:

  • added in the new object
  • removed from the old object
  • changed between old and new
Fields listed in {@code passoverFields} are ignored.

Notes:

  • For changed/added values the method stores a resolved representation using {@link #getUpdatedEntityName(Object, String)}.
  • The method iterates directly over the underlying maps to avoid creating intermediate collections and to minimize memory overhead.
  • Callers should ensure {@code oldProps.getJsonObject(key)} and {@code newProps.getJsonObject(key)} are non-null before invoking this method.

The EventReceiver class subscribes to topics & receives events from different sources using ZeroMQ's PULL socket.

This class is responsible for:

  • Receiving and decrypting messages from various sources
  • Routing messages to appropriate handlers via the Vert.x event bus
  • Handling different message types and topics (agent events, manager events, remote event processor events, datastore events, etc.)
  • Managing high-water marks to control message buffering
  • Processing events in a dedicated thread to avoid blocking the main event loop

The EventReceiver binds to a specified port and receives messages from senders. It then processes these messages based on their topic and content, routing them to the appropriate handlers within the system. Example usage:

    private void assertAssignObjectTestResult(VertxTestContext testContext, long id, int size)
    {
        var retries = new AtomicInteger(0);

        TestUtil.vertx().setPeriodic(1000, timer ->
        {
            retries.getAndIncrement();

            var item = RunbookPluginConfigStore.getStore().getItem(id);

            if (item == null)
            {
                TestUtil.vertx().cancelTimer(timer);

                testContext.failNow(new Exception("item not found"));
            }
            else
            {
                if (item.containsKey(RunbookPlugin.RUNBOOK_PLUGIN_CONTEXT))
                {
                    item.mergeIn(item.getJsonObject(RunbookPlugin.RUNBOOK_PLUGIN_CONTEXT));

                    item.remove(RunbookPlugin.RUNBOOK_PLUGIN_CONTEXT);
                }

                Assertions.assertNotNull(item.getJsonArray(RunbookPlugin.RUNBOOK_PLUGIN_ENTITIES));

                if (item.getJsonArray(RunbookPlugin.RUNBOOK_PLUGIN_ENTITIES).size() == size)
                {
                    TestUtil.vertx().cancelTimer(timer);

                    testContext.completeNow();
                }

                if (retries.get() > 5)
                {
                    TestUtil.vertx().cancelTimer(timer);

                    testContext.failNow(new Exception("Runbook plugin entities not match..."));
                }
            }
        });
    }

            var items = RunbookPluginConfigStore.getStore().getItems();

            Assertions.assertNotNull(items);

            var filteredItems = new JsonArray();

            for (var index = 0; index < entities.size(); index++)
            {
                var entity = entities.getJsonObject(index);

                entity.remove(ENTITY_PROPERTY_COUNT);

                entity.remove(RUNBOOK_RUNNABLE);

                entity.remove(DBConstants.FIELD_TYPE);

                if (filters != null)
                {
                    entity.getMap().keySet().removeIf(filters::contains);
                }
                filteredItems.add(CommonUtil.removeSensitiveFields(entity, true));
            }

            var records = new JsonArray();

            for (var index = 0; index < items.size(); index++)
            {
                var item = items.getJsonObject(index);

                item.remove(ENTITY_PROPERTY_COUNT);

                item.remove(DBConstants.FIELD_TYPE);

                records.add(CommonUtil.removeSensitiveFields(item, true));
            }

            Assertions.assertEquals(filteredItems.stream().collect(Collectors.groupingBy(item -> JsonObject.mapFrom(item).getLong(ID), Collectors.toList()))
                    , records.stream().collect(Collectors.groupingBy(item -> JsonObject.mapFrom(item).getLong(ID), Collectors.toList())));

            testContext.completeNow();

        })));
    }

    /**
     * Qualifies an event against applicable policies.
     * This method:
     * 1. Determines the event type (log, flow, trap)
     * 2. Finds applicable policies based on event source and groups
     * 3. Evaluates the event against policy conditions
     * 4. Forwards qualified events to the EventPolicyInspector
     *
     * @param event The event to qualify, containing event data and metadata
     */
    private void qualify(JsonObject event)
    {
        try
        {
            var item = EventSourceConfigStore.getStore().getItemByHost(event.getString(EVENT_SOURCE), false);

            if (item != null)
            {
                for (var entry : assign(item.getJsonArray(LogEngineConstants.SOURCE_GROUPS), event.getString(EVENT_SOURCE), event.getString(LogEngineConstants.EVENT_SOURCE_TYPE)).entrySet())
                {
                    for (var value : entry.getValue())
                    {
                        var policy = policies.get(value);

                        if (policy.getString(POLICY_STATE).equalsIgnoreCase(YES) && !suppressedPolicies.contains(value))
                        {
                            var context = policy.getJsonObject(POLICY_CONTEXT);

                            if (event.containsKey(entry.getKey()) && event.getValue(entry.getKey()) != null)
                            {
                                var valid = !numericColumns.contains(entry.getKey()) || CommonUtil.getLong(event.getValue(entry.getKey())) > 0;

                                if (valid && context.containsKey(POLICY_RESULT_BY) && !context.getJsonArray(POLICY_RESULT_BY).isEmpty())
                                {
                                    for (var i = 0; i < context.getJsonArray(POLICY_RESULT_BY).size(); i++)
                                    {
                                        var counter = context.getJsonArray(POLICY_RESULT_BY).getString(i);

                                        if (!event.containsKey(counter) && !CommonUtil.isNotNullOrEmpty(CommonUtil.getString(event.getValue(counter))))
                                        {
                                            valid = false;
                                        }
                                    }
                                }

                                if (valid)
                                {
                                    var filter = context.getJsonObject(FILTERS).getJsonObject(DATA_FILTER, null);

                                    var groupConditionSatisfied = true;

                                    if (filter != null && !filter.isEmpty())
                                    {
                                            var groupOperator = filter.getString(OPERATOR);

                                            var conditionGroups = filter.getJsonArray(CONDITION_GROUPS);

                                            for (var index = 0; index < conditionGroups.size(); index++)
                                            {
                                                var conditionGroup = conditionGroups.getJsonObject(index);

                                                var operator = conditionGroup.getString(OPERATOR);

                                                var conditions = conditionGroup.getJsonArray(CONDITIONS);

                                                var satisfied = false;

                                                for (var j = 0; j < conditions.size(); j++)
                                                {
                                                    var condition = conditions.getJsonObject(j);

                                                    var operand = condition.getString(OPERAND).contains(CARET_SEPARATOR) ? condition.getString(OPERAND).split(CARET_SEPARATOR_WITH_ESCAPE)[0] : condition.getString(OPERAND);

                                                    if (event.containsKey(operand))
                                                    {
                                                        satisfied = PolicyEngineConstants.evaluateCondition(conditionGroup.getString(FILTER).equalsIgnoreCase("include"), condition.getString(OPERATOR), condition.getValue(VALUE), event.getValue(operand));

                                                        if ((satisfied && operator.equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.ConditionGroup.OR.getName())) || (!satisfied && operator.equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.ConditionGroup.AND.getName())))
                                                        {
                                                            break;
                                                        }
                                                    }
                                                }

                                                if (!satisfied && groupOperator.equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.ConditionGroup.AND.getName()))
                                                {
                                                    //if main condition is "AND" and any counter group condition is not true so breaking for loop as in "AND" condition all condition is needed to be true
                                                    groupConditionSatisfied = false;

                                                    break;
                                                }
                                                else if (satisfied && groupOperator.equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.ConditionGroup.OR.getName()))
                                                {
                                                    //if main condition is "OR" and any counter group condition is true so breaking for loop as in "OR" condition only one condition needed to be true
                                                    groupConditionSatisfied = true;

                                                    break;
                                                }
                                                else if (!satisfied && groupOperator.equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.ConditionGroup.OR.getName()))
                                                {
                                                    groupConditionSatisfied = false;
                                                }
                                            }

                                        if (groupConditionSatisfied)
                                        {
                                            var result = new JsonObject();

                                            //will forward required fields only to inspector
                                            for (var key : filters.get(policy.getLong(ID)))
                                            {
                                                result.put(CommonUtil.getString(key), event.getString(CommonUtil.getString(key)));
                                            }

                                            aggregate(result.put(POLICY_ID, value).put(EVENT_TIMESTAMP, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP)).put(EVENT_COPY_REQUIRED, false));

                                            if (MotadataConfigUtil.devMode())
                                            {
                                                vertx.eventBus().publish(EventBusConstants.EVENT_EVENT_POLICY_TEST, new JsonObject().put(POLICY_ID, value).put(EVENT_TIMESTAMP, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP)).put(EVENT_COPY_REQUIRED, false));
                                            }
                                        }
                                    }
                                    else
                                    {
                                        var result = new JsonObject();

                                        //will forward required fields only to inspector
                                        for (var key : filters.get(policy.getLong(ID)))
                                        {
                                            result.put(CommonUtil.getString(key), event.getString(CommonUtil.getString(key)));
                                        }

                                        aggregate(result.put(POLICY_ID, value).put(EVENT_TIMESTAMP, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP)).put(EVENT_COPY_REQUIRED, false));

                                        if (MotadataConfigUtil.devMode())
                                        {
                                            vertx.eventBus().publish(EventBusConstants.EVENT_EVENT_POLICY_TEST, new JsonObject().put(POLICY_ID, value).put(EVENT_TIMESTAMP, event.getLong(EVENT_TIMESTAMP)).put(EVENT_COPY_REQUIRED, false));
                                        }
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Finds applicable policies for an event based on its source, source type, and groups.
     * This method aggregates policies from different mapping sources to create a complete
     * set of policies that should be evaluated for the event.
     *
     * @param groups          The groups associated with the event source
     * @param source          The event source
     * @param eventSourceType The event source type
     * @return A map of data points to sets of policy IDs that should be evaluated
     */
    private Map<String, Set<Long>> assign(JsonArray groups, String source, String eventSourceType)
    {
        var qualifiedPolicies = new HashMap<String, Set<Long>>();

        try
        {
            policiesBySource.getOrDefault(source, Collections.emptyMap()).forEach((key, policyIds) ->
            {
                if (!policyIds.isEmpty())
                {
                    qualifiedPolicies.computeIfAbsent(key, value -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).addAll(policyIds);
                }
            });


            if (CommonUtil.isNotNullOrEmpty(eventSourceType))
            {
                policiesBySourceType.getOrDefault(eventSourceType, Collections.emptyMap()).forEach((key, policyIds) ->
                {
                    if (!policyIds.isEmpty())
                    {
                        qualifiedPolicies.computeIfAbsent(key, value -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).addAll(policyIds);
                    }
                });
            }

            for (var index = 0; index < groups.size(); index++)
            {
                var group = groups.getLong(index);

                policiesByGroup.getOrDefault(group, Collections.emptyMap()).forEach((key, policyIds) ->
                {
                    if (!policyIds.isEmpty())
                    {
                        qualifiedPolicies.computeIfAbsent(key, value -> new LinkedHashSet<>()).addAll(policyIds);
                    }
                });
            }
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }

        return qualifiedPolicies;
    }

    /**
     * Maps policies to event sources, source types, and groups.
     * This method builds the mapping between policies and the entities they apply to,
     * which is essential for efficient policy qualification.
     */
    private void qualify()
    {
        policiesBySource.clear();

        policiesByGroup.clear();

        policiesBySourceType.clear();

        try
        {
            policies.forEach((key, value) ->
            {
                var policyContext = value.getJsonObject(POLICY_CONTEXT);

                var dataPoint = policyContext.getString(VisualizationConstants.DATA_POINT);

                JsonArray entities;

                if (policyContext.getJsonArray(ENTITIES) != null && !policyContext.getJsonArray(ENTITIES).isEmpty())//if policy contains filter of group or monitor so just assigning that filtered entities or groups
                {
                    entities = policyContext.getJsonArray(ENTITIES);

                    if (policyContext.getString(ENTITY_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(APIConstants.Entity.GROUP.getName()))
                    {
                        assignById(value.getLong(ID), dataPoint, entities, policiesByGroup);
                    }
                    else if (policyContext.getString(ENTITY_TYPE).equalsIgnoreCase(VisualizationConstants.VisualizationGrouping.EVENT_SOURCE_TYPE.getName()))
                    {
                        assignBySource(value.getLong(ID), dataPoint, entities, policiesBySourceType);
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        assignBySource(value.getLong(ID), dataPoint, entities, policiesBySource);
                    }
                }
                else
                {
                    if (dataPoint.equalsIgnoreCase(MESSAGE) || dataPoint.equalsIgnoreCase(LogEngineConstants.EVENT_CATEGORY) || dataPoint.equalsIgnoreCase(LogEngineConstants.EVENT_SOURCE_TYPE) || dataPoint.equalsIgnoreCase(EVENT_SOURCE))
                    {
                        entities = EventSourceConfigStore.getStore().flatItems(EVENT_SOURCE);
                    }
                    else if (!eventColumns.isEmpty() && eventColumns.containsKey(dataPoint))
                    {
                        entities = EventSourceConfigStore.getStore().flatItemsByMultiValueFields(EVENT_TYPE, value.getString(POLICY_TYPE).toLowerCase(), EVENT_SOURCE, PLUGIN_ID, eventColumns.getJsonObject(dataPoint).getJsonArray(DatastoreConstants.MAPPER_PLUGIN_IDS));
                    }
                    else entities = new JsonArray();

                    assignBySource(value.getLong(ID), dataPoint, entities, policiesBySource);
                }
            });
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }

    }

    /**
     * Aggregates an event against in-memory policies.
     * <p>
     * This method evaluates an incoming event against applicable policies stored in memory.
     * It handles different types of events including traps and regular events, and manages
     * the policy evaluation lifecycle.
     *
     * @param event The event to inspect
     */
    private void aggregate(JsonObject event) // inspect for in-memory policies
    {
        try
        {

            var policy = policies.get(event.getLong(POLICY_ID));

            if (policy != null)
            {
                var context = policy.getJsonObject(POLICY_CONTEXT);

                if (!event.containsKey(EVENT_TIMESTAMP))
                {
                    event.put(EVENT_TIMESTAMP, DateTimeUtil.currentSeconds());
                }

                if (context.containsKey(POLICY_RESULT_BY) && !context.getJsonArray(POLICY_RESULT_BY).isEmpty())
                {
                    var stats = policyGroupStats.get(policy.getLong(ID));

                    if (stats.size() > MAX_GROUPS)
                    {
                        LOGGER.warn(String.format("policy: %s, Unique groups are more than %d, increase max group count or configure policy", policy.getString(POLICY_NAME), MAX_GROUPS));

                        var values = new ArrayList<>(stats.values());

                        var aggregator = context.getString(VisualizationConstants.AGGREGATOR);

                        LogParser.GroupStatSorter.sort(values, aggregator, TOP_N_GROUPS);

                        stats.clear();

                        for (var value : values)
                        {
                            stats.put(value.group, value);
                        }
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        var groupByFields = context.getJsonArray(POLICY_RESULT_BY);

                        var addGroupingCounters = false;

                        if (!groupingCounters.containsKey(policy.getLong(ID)))
                        {
                            groupingCounters.put(policy.getLong(ID), new String[4]);

                            addGroupingCounters = true;
                        }

                        // Switched from StringBuilder to StringJoiner for cleaner and slightly more efficient handling of delimited string construction in loops.
                        var joiner = new StringJoiner(COLUMN_SEPARATOR);

                        for (var i = 0; i < groupByFields.size(); i++)
                        {
                            joiner.add(String.valueOf(event.getValue(groupByFields.getString(i))));

                            if (addGroupingCounters)
                            {
                                groupingCounters.get(policy.getLong(ID))[i] = groupByFields.getString(i);
                            }
                        }

                        var groupingKey = joiner.toString();

                        var stat = stats.computeIfAbsent(groupingKey, LogParser.GroupStat::new);

                        stat.count++;

                        if (context.getString(VisualizationConstants.AGGREGATOR).equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.AggregationType.SUM.getName())
                                || context.getString(VisualizationConstants.AGGREGATOR).equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.AggregationType.AVG.getName()))
                        {
                            stat.sum += CommonUtil.getLong(event.getValue(context.getString(VisualizationConstants.DATA_POINT)));
                        }
                    }
                }
                else
                {
                    // simple policy (no group by)
                    var stats = policyGroupStats.computeIfAbsent(policy.getLong(ID), k -> new HashMap<>());

                    var stat = stats.computeIfAbsent("default", LogParser.GroupStat::new);

                    stat.count++;

                    if (context.getString(VisualizationConstants.AGGREGATOR).equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.AggregationType.SUM.getName())
                            || context.getString(VisualizationConstants.AGGREGATOR).equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.AggregationType.AVG.getName()))
                    {
                        stat.sum += CommonUtil.getLong(event.getValue(context.getString(VisualizationConstants.DATA_POINT)));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Inner class for tracking statistics for a group in policy evaluation.
     * <p>
     * This class maintains the group identifier, sum of values, and count of events
     * for calculating aggregations like sum, average, and count.
     */
    private static class GroupStat
    {
        /**
         * The group identifier
         */
        final String group;

        /**
         * Sum of values for this group
         */
        long sum;

        /**
         * Count of events for this group
         */
        int count;

        /**
         * Constructs a new GroupStat for the specified group.
         *
         * @param group The group identifier
         */
        GroupStat(String group)
        {
            this.group = group;
        }

        /**
         * Calculates the average value for this group.
         *
         * @return The average value, or 0 if count is 0
         */
        long avg()
        {
            return count == 0 ? 0 : sum / count;
        }
    }

    /**
     * Utility class for sorting group statistics.
     * <p>
     * This class provides methods for sorting group statistics based on different
     * aggregation criteria and limiting the results to the top N groups.
     */
    private static class GroupStatSorter
    {
        /**
         * Sorts a list of group statistics and keeps only the top N groups.
         * <p>
         * This method uses a priority queue to efficiently find the top N groups
         * based on the specified aggregator (sum, avg, or count) without sorting the entire list.
         *
         * @param values     The list of group statistics to sort
         * @param aggregator The aggregation type to use for sorting (sum, avg, or count)
         * @param topN       The number of top groups to keep
         */
        public static void sort(List<LogParser.GroupStat> values, String aggregator, int topN)
        {
            Comparator<LogParser.GroupStat> comparator;

            if (aggregator.equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.AggregationType.SUM.getName()))
            {
                comparator = Comparator.comparingLong((LogParser.GroupStat stat) -> stat.sum).reversed();
            }
            else if (aggregator.equalsIgnoreCase(DatastoreConstants.AggregationType.AVG.getName()))
            {
                comparator = Comparator.comparingLong(LogParser.GroupStat::avg).reversed();
            }
            else
            {
                comparator = Comparator.comparingInt((LogParser.GroupStat stat) -> stat.count).reversed();
            }

            // Use Priority Queue for optimal TopK performance
            sort(values, comparator, topN);
        }

        /**
         * Uses a priority queue to efficiently find the top K elements.
         * <p>
         * This approach maintains a min-heap of size K, which significantly outperforms
         * traditional sorting for large datasets. The priority queue only keeps the K largest
         * elements seen so far, making it very memory efficient and fast.
         *
         * @param values     List of GroupStat objects to process
         * @param comparator Comparator to use for sorting
         * @param k          Number of top elements to keep
         */
        private static void sort(List<LogParser.GroupStat> values,
                                 Comparator<LogParser.GroupStat> comparator,
                                 int k)
        {
            if (values.isEmpty() || k <= 0)
            {
                return;
            }

            if (values.size() <= k)
            {
                // If we have fewer elements than k, just sort the list
                values.sort(comparator);

                return;
            }

            // Create a min heap with the reverse of our comparator
            // This keeps the K largest elements with the smallest at the top for easy replacement
            var queue = new PriorityQueue<>(k, comparator.reversed());

            // Process each element
            for (var value : values)
            {
                if (queue.size() < k)
                {
                    // If we haven't reached capacity, add the element
                    queue.offer(value);
                }
                else if (comparator.compare(value, queue.peek()) > 0)
                {
                    // If this element is larger than the smallest in our heap, replace it
                    queue.poll();

                    queue.offer(value);
                }
            }

            // Clear the original list
            values.clear();

            // Convert heap to array for sorting
            var elements = queue.toArray(new LogParser.GroupStat[0]);

            // Sort the result in the desired order
            Arrays.sort(elements, comparator);

            // Add the sorted elements back to the list
            Collections.addAll(values, elements);
        }


    }

            }
        }
        catch (Exception exception)
        {
            LOGGER.error(exception);
        }

        return policy;
    }

        {

                    .add(stat.sum)
                    .add(stat.group));
        }

Implementation of the Notification abstract class for sending Slack notifications.

This class handles Slack notifications by sending HTTP requests to the Slack Web API. It supports:

  • Sending messages to multiple Slack channels in parallel
  • Circuit breaker pattern to handle Slack service failures
  • OAuth token authentication with automatic token refresh
  • Severity-based color coding of messages
  • Configurable timeout for Slack API requests
  • Automatic image upload and attachment for messages with images

The notification process:

  1. Retrieves Slack integration configuration from the configuration store
  2. Validates that channels are specified and Slack integration is configured
  3. For each channel, retrieves the channel configuration and credential profile
  4. Formats the message with severity-based color coding
  5. Checks if image upload is required and handles file upload if needed
  6. Sends HTTP requests to the Slack API for each channel
  7. Handles authentication failures by refreshing OAuth tokens
  8. Tracks successful deliveries and reports results

The notification event should contain:

  • {@link PolicyEngineConstants#CHANNELS}: JsonArray of channel IDs to send the message to
  • {@link Notification#CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_CONTENT}: The message content in Slack Block Kit format
  • {@link GlobalConstants#SEVERITY} (optional): The severity level for color coding
  • {@code imageAttached} (optional): Boolean flag indicating if image upload is required

The message content is provided as a complete Slack Block Kit JSON template from the PolicyEngine, with all variables already substituted. This class simply adds the channel information and sends the message to the Slack API.

This implementation uses a circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures when the Slack service is experiencing issues.

This method is responsible for transforming raw metric data from database queries into visualization-ready format for different chart types (Histogram, Grid, etc.). It performs several key operations:

Core Functionality:

  • Data Transformation: Converts raw query results into visualization context
  • Aggregation Processing: Handles MIN, MAX, SUM, AVG aggregations for metrics
  • Entity Resolution: Resolves monitor IDs, groups, and tags for visualization grouping
  • Chart Context Creation: Builds appropriate visualization context based on category
  • Statistical Calculations: Computes grid statistics for histogram data

Supported Visualization Categories:

  • HISTOGRAM: Creates chart context with sorting and statistical aggregations
  • GRID: Creates grid context for tabular data display

Entity Grouping Support:

  • MONITOR: Groups by individual monitoring objects
  • GROUP: Groups by object groups
  • TAG: Groups by user-defined tags

Data Processing Flow:

  1. Extract visualization properties and sorting preferences
  2. Determine entity type (monitor/group/tag) from context
  3. Process raw data rows and calculate statistics if needed
  4. Resolve entity IDs and build entity collections
  5. Transform data points with aggregation support
  6. Build final visualization context and send to event bus

Error Handling:

The ReportCleanupJob class is responsible for cleaning up old report files in the Motadata platform.

This class implements the Quartz Job interface and performs regular cleanup of report files to prevent excessive disk usage. Reports are generated for various purposes in the platform, and old reports need to be periodically cleaned up to avoid accumulation of unnecessary files.

The job performs the following tasks:

  1. Calculates a timestamp for 1 hour ago
  2. Lists all files in the uploads/reports directory
  3. Deletes any files that are older than 1 hour

The job is scheduled to run every hour to ensure regular cleanup of report files.

The EventTracker class tracks the status and progress of events as they flow through the system.

This class is responsible for:

  • Adding events to a tracking queue with timestamps and initial state
  • Updating event progress and state as they move through the system
  • Completing events with success, failure, or abort status
  • Maintaining a limited-size cache of recent events for monitoring and debugging
  • Providing event context information to requesting components
  • Streaming event updates to clients in real-time
  • Logging event details when logging is enabled

The EventTracker maintains a fixed-size cache of events, removing the oldest events when the cache reaches its capacity limit. Each event is tracked with its state, progress log, context information, and other metadata.

The class supports real-time streaming of event updates to clients, which can be enabled or disabled through change notification events. When streaming is enabled, all event updates are broadcast to subscribed clients.

Example usage: 

   // Add a new event to the tracker   JsonObject event = new JsonObject()       .put(EVENT_ID, CommonUtil.newEventId())       .put(EVENT_TYPE, "discovery")       .put(EVENT_CONTEXT, new JsonObject()           .put(OBJECT_IP, "192.168.1.1")           .put(OBJECT_NAME, "router-1"));     vertx.eventBus().send(EVENT_ADD, event);     // Update event progress   JsonObject update = new JsonObject()       .put(EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EVENT_ID))       .put(EVENT_PROGRESS_LOG, "Discovered 5 interfaces");     vertx.eventBus().send(EVENT_PROGRESS_UPDATE, update);     // Complete the event with success   JsonObject complete = new JsonObject()       .put(EVENT_ID, event.getLong(EVENT_ID))       .put(EVENT_CONTEXT, new JsonObject()           .put("discoveredDevices", 10));     vertx.eventBus().send(EVENT_SUCCEED, complete);

  • Connecting to remote endpoints for event forwarding
  • Encrypting and compressing messages before transmission

  • Managing connection lifecycle and error handling

Processes dependency queries and builds dependency hierarchies.

The DependencyQueryProcessor is responsible for:

  • Processing dependency queries received through the event bus
  • Building different types of dependency hierarchies (bottom-top, top-bottom)
  • Handling different categories of objects (network, cloud, virtualization, etc.)
  • Building connections between objects based on their dependencies
  • Supporting different dependency formats (flat, hierarchical)

This processor works with the DependencyManager to retrieve dependency information and build appropriate dependency structures based on query parameters. The resulting dependency hierarchies are used for topology visualization, correlation, and root cause analysis.

The processor supports three main dependency formats:

  • FLAT: Raw dependency connections, primarily used for root cause analysis
  • BOTTOM_TOP_HIERARCHY: Child-to-parent relationships, showing dependencies upward
  • TOP_BOTTOM_HIERARCHY: Parent-to-child relationships, showing dependencies downward

  1. Default User: If the user ID is DEFAULT_ID, returns all group IDs in the system
  2. User Profile with GROUP scope: If the user has a profile with GROUP scope type, returns the groups defined in the profile context
  3. User Profile with other scope types: If the user has a profile with non-GROUP scope (e.g., TAG), returns an empty array as groups are not applicable
  4. Direct Group Assignment: If the user has no profile or an invalid profile, returns the groups directly assigned to the user

  • Determining which groups can be selected in group-based policies
  • Building hierarchical group trees for user interfaces

Utility class for managing file-based shutdown mechanisms on Windows systems.

This class provides a cross-process shutdown coordination mechanism specifically designed for Windows environments where multiple Motadata processes need to be gracefully terminated. It implements a file-based signaling system that allows external processes, services, or system administrators to trigger controlled application shutdown.

Key Features:

  • File-based shutdown watcher that monitors for shutdown signals
  • Periodic monitoring with configurable intervals (default: 1 second)
  • Asynchronous file operations using Vert.x file system API
  • Graceful shutdown coordination across multiple processes
  • Windows-specific implementation with OS validation

Workflow:

  1. Initialize shutdown watcher using {@link #initShutdownWatcher()}
  2. Watcher periodically checks for shutdown file existence and content
  3. External processes write shutdown signal using {@link #writeShutdownSignal()}
  4. When "shutdown" keyword is detected, application terminates gracefully

File Structure: 

   {CURRENT_DIR}/shutdown/shutdown.ctx

Usage Example: 

   // Initialize shutdown watcher (typically in Bootstrap)   ShutdownUtil.initShutdownWatcher(vertx);     // Trigger shutdown from another process   ShutdownUtil.writeShutdownSignal(vertx)       .onSuccess(v -> logger.info("Shutdown signal sent"))       .onFailure(throwable -> logger.error("Failed to send shutdown signal", throwable));

Thread Safety: This class uses static methods and maintains internal state through static variables. The {@code running} flag is used to coordinate shutdown across multiple timer instances.

Platform Compatibility: Currently supports Windows systems only. Non-Windows platforms will log a debug message and skip initialization.

This method delegates the connection operation to the underlying transport client and, upon successful connection, starts a periodic timer to check the connection health. If the connection has been idle for longer than the configured timeout, a reconnection attempt will be made.

The connection process:

  1. Registers the message handler to track message activity
  2. Delegates the connection operation to the underlying client
  3. Upon successful connection, starts the connection health check timer

The connection health check:

  • Runs at the interval specified by {@link #REMOTE_SESSION_PROBE_MILLIS}
  • Checks if the time since the last message exceeds {@link #RECONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}
  • If the timeout is exceeded, verifies that the remote endpoint is reachable
  • If reachable, initiates a reconnection attempt

  • Listening for and responding to events regarding the state of the datastore (e.g., up or down).

  • Managing event retention and initiating retention operations based on retention policies.

  • Supports High Availability (HA) environments, sending events either to a local datastore or to a primary datastore, depending on the mode.

The LogParser is a central component of the log processing system that handles the parsing of log data from various sources. It supports multiple parsing strategies:

  • Regex-based parsing - Uses regular expressions to extract fields from log messages
  • JSON parsing - Parses structured JSON log messages
  • Delimiter-based parsing - Splits log messages using a specified delimiter
  • Custom plugin-based parsing - Uses custom plugins for specialized log formats

Key features:

  • Maintains maps of parsers, patterns, and other metadata
  • Filters logs based on keywords and source
  • Parses logs using different strategies
  • Enriches log data with additional information
  • Handles the loading and compilation of parser plugins
  • Flushes parsed logs to storage

The LogParser integrates with the Vert.x event bus system for communication with other components.

This factory method examines the configuration to determine which transport server implementation to instantiate. The transport protocol is specified in the configuration using the {@link EventBusConstants#TRANSPORT_PROTOCOL} key.

Currently supported transport server implementations:

  • {@link ZMQServer} - For ZeroMQ transport protocol

The configuration object should contain all necessary parameters for the specific transport implementation, such as:

  • Host address to bind to
  • Port number
  • Socket mode (PUB, PULL, etc.)
  • Protocol-specific options (high water mark, etc.)

In `RemoteEventRouter.clear()`: Clears event-related resources after processing or timeout.

This method is called when an event has been processed (successfully or with errors) or when an event has timed out. It:

1. Removes the event from tracking maps (remainingEventProcessors, eventAcks) 2. Retrieves and removes the event context 3. Sends a reply if the event requires one 4. Updates event processor statistics if requested 5. Records latency information for the event processor if available

This cleanup ensures that resources are properly released after event processing and that performance metrics are updated for future load balancing decisions. @param event The event context containing event ID and other metadata @param updateEventProcessor Whether to update event processor statistics

In `AuditUtil.updateContext()`: Processes differences between two inner JsonObject contexts identified by {@code key}.

Compares entries of {@code oldProps.getJsonObject(key)} and {@code newProps.getJsonObject(key)} and updates {@code previousContext} and {@code updatedContext} with keys that were:

  • added in the new object
  • removed from the old object
  • changed between old and new
Fields listed in {@code passoverFields} are ignored.

Notes:

  • For changed/added values the method stores a resolved representation using {@link #getUpdatedEntityName(Object, String)}.
  • The method iterates directly over the underlying maps to avoid creating intermediate collections and to minimize memory overhead.
  • Callers should ensure {@code oldProps.getJsonObject(key)} and {@code newProps.getJsonObject(key)} are non-null before invoking this method.
@param key the property name that holds the inner JsonObject to compare @param oldProps JsonObject containing the previous state (parent object) @param newProps JsonObject containing the updated state (parent object) @param previousContext JsonObject to populate with previous values for changed/removed keys @param updatedContext JsonObject to populate with updated values for changed/added keys @param passoverFields optional JsonArray of field names to ignore during comparison; may be null OPTIMIZATION: Process inner context changes without nested streams Replaces Stream.concat().collect().stream() pattern with direct iteration

EventEngine is a core component for event processing and distribution in the Motadata platform. It provides a flexible and scalable mechanism for handling events across the system with support for:
  • Local and remote event processing
  • Event forwarding to other components
  • Persistent event storage with offset tracking
  • Blocking and non-blocking event handling
  • Back-pressure management to prevent system overload
  • Event segmentation for improved performance

The EventEngine uses a producer-consumer pattern where events are produced and stored, then consumed by handlers based on system capacity. It integrates with Vert.x event bus for internal communication and ZeroMQ for external communication.
